name: Sinhagad Hills & Ridge
habitatType: Dry Deciduous & Moist Western Ghats Scrub

climateSummary.microclimate: High-altitude ridge with rapid moisture evaporative loss during dry breaks
primaryThreats: Pre-monsoon soil desiccations
Invasive weed encroachment (Lantana camara)
Fringe tourism vehicular heat & road expansion

description: Rising to over 1,300 meters southwest of Pune city, the Sinhagad spur serves as an essential ecological stepping stone connecting the Sahyadri crest to the interior Deccan plateau. Its moist ravines harbor endangered micro-endemic amphibians and raptor nesting ledges that face acute desiccating stress from prolonged post-monsoon heat spells.

name: Pashan Lake & Riparian Wetland

climateSummary.rainfallAnomaly: +22% flash runoff intensity with longer dry intervals
climateSummary.microclimate: Shallow urban wetland experiencing eutrophic surface warming & dissolved oxygen crashes
primaryThreats: Rapid water hyacinth blooming during heat spikes
Siltation from upstream catchment real-estate construction
Nighttime urban glare affecting migratory waterfowl

description: Constructed in the British era on Ramnadi to supply water to the Kirkee cantonment, Pashan Lake has served for decades as a vital wintering stopover for Central Asian Flyway waterfowl. Rising water surface temperatures and urban runoff storm surges have exacerbated catastrophic dissolved oxygen depletion, decimating benthic food webs.

name: Mulshi Catchment & Sahyadri Rim
habitatType: Subtropical Wet Evergreen & Moist Mixed Deciduous

climateSummary.rainfallAnomaly: +34% erratic cloudburst frequency followed by sudden rain lulls
climateSummary.microclimate: Orographic precipitation belt on Western Ghats crest with sensitive moist evergreen pockets
primaryThreats: Flash landslides stripping steep topsoil
Resort developments severing contiguous tree canopy
Dry winter humidity drops affecting epiphytic orchids and lichens

description: Positioned along the heavy orographic rainfall edge of the northern Western Ghats, Mulshi harbors high floral and insect endemism. While overall monsoon totals remain high, extreme torrential episodes interspersed with extended dry breaks prevent stable sapling recruitment in native semi-evergreen climax species.

name: Vetal & Taljai Tekdi Complex
habitatType: Deciduous Thorn Scrub & Lateritic Grassland Plateau

climateSummary.rainfallAnomaly: -18% ground percolation efficiency due to compacted urban periphery
climateSummary.microclimate: Elevated urban ridge acting as Pune city's major ecological lung and thermal buffer
primaryThreats: Summer wild grass fires stoked by high wind and thermal spikes
Exotic monoculture plantation (Gliricidia sepium) choking native flora
Habitat dissection by urban road proposals

description: The prominent hillock complex standing in western central Pune is the city's green heart. The rocky laterite plateaus and thorn scrub patches support specialized xeric plants, rare ground-nesting birds, and endemic succulents that are vulnerable to early seasonal drying and invasive weed propagation.

name: Bhimashankar Corridor Buffer Zone
habitatType: Northern Western Ghats Moist Semi-Evergreen Sanctuary

climateSummary.microclimate: Perpetual cloud-forest moisture zone during monsoon, vulnerable to spring heat pulses
primaryThreats: Canopy disconnectivity affecting arboreal species
Fruiting phenology shift in native ficus and myristica trees
High seasonal forest fire risks on periphery

description: Northern tip of the Pune forest division, this buffer zone safeguards the iconic Maharashtra state animal, the Malabar Giant Squirrel. Climate-induced alterations in fruiting schedules of canopy trees are forcing arboreal mammals closer to ground levels, heightening predation and roadkill risks.

name: Panshet & Varasgaon Valleys
habitatType: River Valley Riparian Zone & High-Gradient Catchment

climateSummary.microclimate: Interlocking reservoir hill slopes subject to heavy seasonal shoreline expansion and retreat
primaryThreats: Shoreline erosion exposing breeding burrows
Rapid drawdown of reservoir waters during extended heat spells
Submersion and displacement of riparian scrub

description: Supplying municipal water to millions in Pune, the Panshet and Varasgaon dam valleys are flanked by secondary moist deciduous growth. Sharp swings between erratic reservoir high-water marks and prolonged dry drawdowns severely disrupt reptile nesting and riparian amphibian lifecycles.

name: Mula-Mutha River Basin
habitatType: Urban Riparian Floodplain & Degraded Alluvial Riverbanks

climateSummary.rainfallAnomaly: +40% instantaneous peak discharge during cloudburst events
climateSummary.microclimate: Severely degraded urban hydrological corridor with extreme water temperatures in summer
primaryThreats: Combined sewage discharge causing anoxic conditions
Loss of natural riverbank sand bars and reed beds
Thermal pollution killing native fish and aquatic insect fry

description: Flowing through the belly of metropolitan Pune, the confluence of the Mula and Mutha rivers represents the region's most stressed freshwater ecosystem. Rapid channelization, combined with urban heat surges and flood pulses, has wiped out over 60% of indigenous Deccan freshwater fish species.

name: Urban Pune Green Corridors
habitatType: Historic Heritage Botanical Gardens & Canopy Tree Roosts

climateSummary.rainfallAnomaly: +4.2°C Urban Heat Island (UHI) temperature differential over surrounding rural zones
climateSummary.microclimate: Pronounced urban heat dome with reduced nocturnal cooling and high thermal radiation
primaryThreats: Mass mortality of large fruit bats during heatwaves exceeding 42°C
Asphalt radiation preventing ground nesting of beneficial urban insects
Old-growth heritage tree felling for road widening

description: Comprising the expansive campuses of Savitribai Phule Pune University, Empress Botanical Garden, and the Agriculture College, these remnant old-growth groves host critical colonial roosts of fruit bats and urban raptors now routinely threatened by searing pre-monsoon heatwaves.
